Strip war criminals of right to presidential clemency
2014-11-06T00:00:15+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/strip-war-criminals-of-right-to-presidential-clemency-48970

Expressing concern that convicted war criminals might be pardoned following a change in political regime, Ekatturer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee yesterday urged the government to ensure that such persons are stripped of the right to seek presidential clemency.

“We are not asking to curtail the president's power of clemency,” said Tureen Afroze, the committee's law affairs secretary, suggesting making amendments to articles 47 (3) and 47 A of the constitution which limit the fundamental rights of war criminals.

The International War Crimes Tribunal prosecutor was addressing a discussion organised by the committee advocating for war crimes trial at Women's Voluntary Association in the capital's Dhanmondi marking the 42nd anniversary of the constitution's enactment.

Under Article 47 A (1), a person who committed genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes cannot enjoy the right to protection of law provided by Article 31, protection with respect to trial and punishment provided by Article 35 (1) and (5) and the right to move to the High Court for enforcement of fundamental rights provided by Article 44, she said.

Afroze also pointed out that as per Article 47 A (2), war criminals, including Jamaat-e-Islami leader Kamaruzzaman whose death penalty was recently upheld by the Supreme Court, cannot file review petitions.

The nirmul committee's acting president, renowned writer and journalist Shahriar Kabir reemphasised the need to ban Jamaat-e-Islami, referring to Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's speech on November 8, 1972 while placing the draft constitution before the national assembly.

He said secularism had been kept as one of the constitution's pillars so that none could use religion as a political tool.

Barrister Amir-ul Islam, one of those who formulated the constitution, also spoke at the programme chaired by former judge Syed Amirul Islam, an adviser of the committee.
